reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) strongly supports the fluorine effect on Ti-45Al-8.5Nb, but the hypothesis extends this mechanism to a chemically distinct HfNbTaTiZr alloy without any cited evidence for fluoride volatility, oxide composition, or mechanical property retention in that system. The key premise of transferability is unsupported, and the mechanism is only loosely related to the cited TiAl results.
premises: Fluorine surface treatment promotes formation of a protective Al2O3 film on TiAl alloys at 1000 °C
The protective film significantly reduces oxidation weight gain (e.g., from 6.03 to 0.81 mg/cm²)
The film is continuous, adherent, and forms during isothermal oxidation up to 100 h
The fluorine effect mechanism involves volatile metal fluorides that react with oxygen to nucleate the protective scale
This treatment can be directly transferred to HfNbTaTiZr to form a protective oxide without degrading mechanical properties
